title: RackWalker scene contract
description: Source of truth for every body exchanged between web/ and proxy/. Contract version 2.5.0 (2.0.0, the first public contract, plus the game shell: player sessions and game state; 2.2.0 added the site country for the overworld; 2.3.0 adds quests: the gap scanner, quest lines, rewards, the practice island, and the change ops a quest line ends in). Change only by contract change; see contracts/README.md.

IsoCoord.description: Tile coordinate on the parent grid; null = not placed yet (the engine auto-lays out, deterministically, and never writes that back unless the user drags).

IsoSize.description: Size in tiles; null = engine default.

IsoFacing.description: Grid direction the front faces. N = -y (screen up-right), E = +x (screen down-right), S = +y (screen down-left), W = -x (screen up-left). See contracts/iso.md.

NetboxUrl.description: Absolute link to the object in the NetBox web UI (for 'open in NetBox'); null when unknown.

PortKind.description: Short name of the NetBox termination model (dcim.interface -> interface, dcim.frontport -> front_port, circuits.circuittermination -> circuit_termination, ...). (kind, id) is unique; id alone is not.

netbox_version.description: Version reported by NetBox /api/status/, e.g. 4.7.4; null for fixtures.

source.description: cache = served from the proxy read cache.

status.description: NetBox status value: planned|staging|active|decommissioning|retired (sites may define more).

iso_theme.description: Custom field iso_theme; null = app default theme.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the site (custom field iso_country, else the site's own region as a two-letter code or a country name, else the last line of its physical address); null = unknown. Picks the overworld's landmark and villager set.

unracked_devices.description: Devices in the site with rack_id null or position null (0U devices count here too).

cables.description: Cables with at least one termination in the site.

Location.description: A NetBox Location, drawn as a room. iso_* are custom fields; coordinates are tiles on the site grid.

parent_id.description: Parent location (NetBox locations nest); null = top level.

iso_facing.description: Side of the room that has the door.

Rack.description: A NetBox Rack. One tile footprint. iso_x/iso_y are tiles on the location grid (relative to the location origin) or on the site grid when location_id is null.

starting_unit.description: Number of the lowest U (NetBox default 1).

desc_units.description: true when units are numbered top to bottom.

slug.description: Sprite choice keys off the slug: switch, router, firewall, server, patch-panel, pdu (others fall back to device_<n>u).

color.description: NetBox role colour, lower-case hex without #.

position.description: Lowest U occupied; null with rack_id set = zero-U / non-racked in that rack.

Termination.description: One end of a cable or a trace hop.

name.description: Port name; for a circuit termination the side, A or Z.

site_id.description: Lets the engine see that a cable leaves the site.

Interface.description: Any cable-able port of a device (an interface in the wide sense); kind also covers patch-panel front/rear ports, console and power ports.

enabled.description: Always true for kinds without an enabled flag.

mgmt_only.description: Always false for kinds other than interface.

link_peers.description: The far side of this port's own cable (one hop).

connected_endpoint.description: End of the whole path through patch panels/circuits (NetBox connected_endpoints[0]); null if the path is incomplete or the kind has none.

type.description: cat6, mmf-om4, smf-os2, dac-passive, power, ... (NetBox cable type).

color.description: Lower-case hex without #; null = theme wire colour.

TraceHop.description: One segment of NetBox's /trace/: near end(s) -> cable -> far end(s).

cable.description: null for a segment with no cable (e.g. a circuit's provider network).

far_end.description: Empty when the path stops here.

hops.description: In order from the origin. A port with no cable (NetBox /trace/ returns []) has hops [], is_complete false, is_split false; the origin is still set.

is_complete.description: The path reaches an endpoint (interface, console/power endpoint, provider network).

is_split.description: The path fans out (e.g. a rear port with several positions); hops stop at the split.

WorldLink.description: Aggregated connectivity between two sites, drawn as one overworld wire. a_site_id < b_site_id.

cable_ids.description: Cables whose two ends are in these two sites.

status.description: ok = NetBox reachable, supported and answered /api/status/ within 2 s; degraded = reachable but unsupported version, or /api/status/ took longer than 2 s (slow); down = unreachable (no answer within 5 s, or not HTTP 200).

write_enabled.description: true only when the proxy runs with WRITE_ENABLED=1.

supported.description: Version is in the supported range (4.7.x for contract 2.4.0).

permission_check.description: Can the proxy's token read NetBox users and object permissions? Both are needed before any write: 'cannot_view_users' or 'cannot_view_permissions' mean every write is refused until the proxy's NetBox user is given view on that type; 'unknown' when NetBox was not reachable (and in fixture mode).

SiteScene.description: GET /api/scene/site/{id}. Feeds zoom levels 'site' and 'room' (room = filter by location_id client-side).

devices.description: All devices of the site, racked or not.

cables.description: Cables with at least one termination in the site; terminations elsewhere carry their own site_id.

devices.description: Devices with rack_id = this rack (position null = zero-U).

cables.description: Cables touching any device in the rack.

DeviceDetail.description: GET /api/device/{id}. Feeds zoom level 'device' and the info panel.

interfaces.description: All ports of every kind. Ordered by kind in PortKind enum order (interface, front_port, rear_port, console_port, ...), then within a kind in the order NetBox's own list endpoint returns them for this device (`GET /api/dcim/<ports>/?device_id=<id>`, NetBox's natural order, e.g. Gi1/0/24, Te1/1/1, mgmt0).

cables.description: Cables attached to any of these ports.

Ref.description: Reference to an object created by an earlier op in the same ChangeSet: '@' + that op's client_ref.

client_ref.description: Optional; unique within the ChangeSet; echoed in the result; lets later ops point at a created object as '@<client_ref>'.

if_unmodified_since.description: Optional optimistic lock: the target's last_updated as the client saw it. A newer last_updated in NetBox makes the op fail with code 'conflict'.

UnplaceDeviceOp.description: Clears rack, position and face; the device stays in its site and location.

UpdateFieldsOp.description: Edit plain fields. The proxy accepts only the whitelist in contracts/api.md#update_fields per kind and answers validation_failed for anything else.

ChangeSet.description: Body of POST /api/changes/preview and POST /api/changes/apply. Ops run in order.

reason.description: Optional note; the proxy logs it with the apply.

id.description: Resolved target. Preview: the request's id, or the request's '@<client_ref>' string unchanged when the target was created by an earlier op of the same ChangeSet; null for create_rack. Apply: always the real NetBox id.

status.description: skipped = not run because an earlier op failed during apply.

before.description: The touched fields before (contract field names); null for create_rack.

after.description: The touched fields after (predicted in preview, read back from NetBox after apply).

applied.description: true only if mode=apply and every op ended ok/no_change.

PlayerId.description: The player's NetBox user id; 0 only in the single-user local mode (RACKWALKER_LOCAL_PLAYER=1).

Player.description: The signed-in player: a NetBox user, as NetBox reported it at sign-in.

display_name.description: NetBox first and last name, or null when NetBox has neither.

GameSession.description: Who is playing. GET /api/game/session always answers 200 with this body.

csrf_token.description: Send it back as the X-RackWalker-CSRF header on every game write. null when signed out.

local_mode.description: true when the proxy runs the single-user local mode (no NetBox sign-in; off by default).

SignInRequest.description: Sign in as a NetBox user with one of that user's NetBox API tokens. The proxy asks NetBox who owns the token, then forgets the token: it is never stored, logged or used again.

HintLevel.description: How often the guide speaks up: off = never on her own (the menu still opens her), low = only first-time essentials, normal = also when you seem stuck, high = also extra tips.

KeyBindings.description: Up to three keys per action. up/down/left/right walk on the overworld; interact talks and chooses, and inside a building enters the selected object; cancel closes and goes back (inside a building: one level out); menu opens the menu; zoom_in, zoom_out, search, rotate (a rack), trace (a port), unrack (a device) and undo (with Ctrl or Cmd held) act inside buildings. Added in 2.2.0 and optional, so settings written before 2.2.0 stay valid: zoom_in, zoom_out, search, rotate, trace, unrack, undo. The proxy fills a missing one with its default (the player's own keys win over a default that clashes with them) on every read and write.

KeyList.description: KeyboardEvent.code values (layout-independent), e.g. ArrowUp, KeyW, Space.

reduce_motion.description: Text appears at once and scene changes cut instead of sliding.

SaveSlotId.description: auto = the autosave slot the game writes on every change of place; 1-3 = manual slots.

SaveData.description: Where the player is. Small on purpose: everything else is re-read from NetBox.

overworld.title: OverworldPos
overworld.description: Overworld tile the player stands on and the way they face.

view.description: The isometric level, in the ?view= deep-link form.

iso.description: The building the player is in (scene iso), else null.

Flags.description: Dialogue and story flags (e.g. ilatea.intro.seen). Open on purpose: names come from the dialogue scripts.

flags.description: Flags to set; null deletes a flag.

GameState.description: Everything the game stores for the signed-in player. Never written into NetBox.

message.description: One human sentence. Never contains the NetBox token.

details.description: Machine detail, e.g. {"field": "position", "reason": "U12 occupied by device 31"}.

ErrorResponse.description: The one error shape for every non-2xx response.

ConnectCableOp.description: A new cable between two ends that have none (2.3.0). An end is a port (kind, id) or a circuit termination; '@<client_ref>' names a termination created earlier in the set.

type.description: A NetBox cable type (cat6, mmf, smf, dac-passive, power, ...). Left out: the cable has no type.

CreateCircuitOp.description: A new circuit of a provider and circuit type (2.3.0); status active. Since 2.5.0 the provider and the type may be '@' references to a create_provider or create_circuit_type op of the same ChangeSet.

CreateCircuitTerminationOp.description: A new end of a circuit (2.3.0): at a site, or (2.4.0) on a network of the circuit's provider. Exactly one of site_id and provider_network_id. The side must be free.

AssignIpOp.description: Puts an address on an interface of the target device (reusing the address object when that interface already has it) and, unless primary is false, makes it the device's primary IP (2.3.0).

CreatePrefixOp.description: A new prefix (2.3.0); refused when that exact prefix exists.

prefix.description: Network with its mask, host bits zero, e.g. 192.0.2.0/24.

QuestRank.description: What a finding is worth: connectivity (can it be reached, and how) before identity (which box is it) before layout (where it stands).

QuestScope.description: netbox = the player's real NetBox; practice = the practice island (synthetic, never written to NetBox).

ObjectRef.description: A NetBox object named as evidence.

Finding.description: Something the estate as a whole does not say yet (docs/quests.md lists the kinds).

Gap.description: One empty field on one object.

Completeness.description: Checks passed out of checks made at a site.

unlisted.description: Expected-cable gaps beyond the per-site cap: counted, not listed.

incomplete.description: Lists the scan could not read in full (capped or refused to the proxy's token); rules that need them stay silent.

GapList.description: One page of a site's gaps, in a fixed order (rank, object type, object id, field).

suggestion.description: A value the label maker proposes; never filled in for the player.

error.description: Why the last answer to this step was not taken.

QuestStep.description: The next question of a quest line.

view.description: The level to open, as in ?view= (rack:5, site:1).

QuestProgress.description: Checks this line stands for, and how many NetBox has confirmed.

purpose.description: Why it matters, in plain words for a site admin.

outcome.description: What the admin can do once the line is complete.

status.description: offered = not started; active = a question is waiting; ready = a change is waiting for preview and apply; parked = the player did not know yet (a field task; no penalty); dismissed = the player says this is how things are; practised = completed as a dry run (no XP); done = NetBox confirms it.

write_blocked.description: Why applying this line's proposal would run as practice for this player (the proxy's mode, or what the player's own NetBox permissions lack); null when it would be written, and when nothing is proposed.

changes.description: The proposal in plain words, one line per op, with the names an admin knows. Empty when nothing is proposed.

checklist.description: What to look for on site while the line is parked.

lapsed.description: Done once, but NetBox no longer shows it. Nothing is reopened; it is only counted.

chain.description: The chain and stage this line belongs to (2.4.0); null for a line outside every chain.

Quest.description: One quest line and where the player stands in it.

QuestGiver.description: The site's quest giver. The game draws them as an animal of the site's country.

boss_ready.description: 100 % complete: the site's Confusion can be faced (the fight comes later).

can_write.description: A real write would be attempted for this player (write-enabled proxy and no known permission problem). Otherwise completions are practice.

queued.description: Open lines not offered yet (at most a few are open per site).

chains.description: Chains in play at the site (or the estate): open ones, those waiting on a fact the player does not know yet, and those the player completed (2.4.0).

chains_queued.description: Chains with something open that are not in play yet (at most a few are open per site).

setup.description: What this NetBox lacks for the game to record everything (custom fields, contact roles), in words (2.4.0). Empty when nothing is lacking.

QuestBoard.description: The quest log: the lines open at a site (or the estate), the player's rewards, and each site's progress.

QuestAnswer.description: One answer to the step a quest line is waiting at: a choice id, a typed text, or form values (blank or absent = not known yet).

verified.description: NetBox (or, on the practice island, the island) was read again and shows the outcome.

trace.description: What NetBox's own cable trace found after a cable was written.

chain.description: The line's chain as it stands after the check (2.4.0).

chain_xp.description: The bonus for a chain NetBox now shows complete, part of xp_awarded (2.4.0).

bonus_xp.description: XP for values that passed a check against the packs (a model the device-type library holds, a serial that fits the vendor's sourced rule), part of xp_awarded (2.5.0). 0 for anything marked unverified.

QuestVerdict.description: What applying or checking a quest line led to.

MgmtMode.description: How a device is managed (2.4.0): locally (it has an address to log in to), by a cloud or controller service (no local address is expected), or not at all. NetBox custom field rw_mgmt_mode on the device.

Money.description: An amount as decimal text, at most two decimals (2.4.0). Never a float.

SetManagementOp.description: Records how a device is managed (2.4.0): custom field rw_mgmt_mode, the service's name in rw_mgmt_service, and optionally the default of the device's model (rw_mgmt_default on its device type; `varies` = each device of the model is asked).

RecordCircuitOp.description: Fills in facts of a circuit's administrative record that NetBox does not hold yet (2.4.0): its provider account, install date, commit rate (kbps), and the charges (custom fields rw_mrc, rw_nrc, rw_currency). A fact NetBox already holds with another value is refused, never overwritten.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of mrc and nrc.

CreateProviderAccountOp.description: A new account with an existing provider (2.4.0). The account number is unique per provider.

CreateProviderNetworkOp.description: A new network of an existing provider (2.4.0), for the far end of a circuit.

CreateContactOp.description: A new contact (2.4.0): a person, a team or a desk.

AssignContactOp.description: Assigns a contact to the target provider or circuit in one of NetBox's contact roles (2.4.0).

ChainStageName.description: physical, logical and administrative are the stages of a record; room, kit and carrier are the stages of setting a site up (2.5.0).

status.description: done = NetBox shows it; answered = what is still open was answered "none, on purpose"; not_known = what is still open was answered "I don't know yet" (it stays an open question and does not count against completeness); open = the stage in play; locked = an earlier stage comes first.

quest_ids.description: The open quest lines that settle this stage.

missing.description: What NetBox does not hold yet, in words.

Chain.description: A quest chain (2.4.0): the quest lines about one subject as a short series of stages, derived from NetBox. A stage NetBox already satisfies is done and never asked; a later stage unlocks when the earlier one is done or answered.

holds.description: What the record will hold when the chain is complete, from the stages this chain has.

bonus_xp.description: The most XP the whole record pays on top of its stages once NetBox shows every stage (QuestVerdict.chain_xp is what was paid: by the share of the stages this player confirmed, and less for a repeat). 0 for a chain of one stage.

status.description: open_questions = nothing left to ask except facts the player does not know yet.

label.description: Where the player is, for example "2 of 3: logical" or "3 of 3: administrative (not known yet: the monthly charge)".

summary.description: The record so far, read from NetBox (or the practice island), in one plain sentence; null while nothing of it is recorded.

SiteOrEstateId.description: A site's NetBox primary key, or 0 for the estate itself: a line about a NetBox that has no site yet (2.5.0).

CreateSiteOp.description: A new site (2.5.0); status active. With `country`, the site gets the region of that country (slug = the code in lower case), which is created when NetBox has none: that is where the game reads a site's country from.

CreateProviderOp.description: A provider (2.5.0), by name, with its AS numbers as NetBox ASN objects (the registry of each is created when missing). A provider NetBox already holds under the same name or slug, or with one of the AS numbers, is matched instead (status no_change; later ops that refer to this op get the existing provider): a provider is never made twice.

aka.description: Other names the provider goes by; used only to match a provider NetBox already holds.

pack.description: The id of the provider pack the entry came from; absent for a name the player typed.

CreateCircuitTypeOp.description: A circuit type (2.5.0), by name; an existing one of that name is matched instead (no_change).

AddDeviceTypeOp.description: A device type in NetBox (2.5.0), with its manufacturer when missing. With `library_file` it is imported from the pinned device-type library: the full definition is fetched, checked against the index's SHA-256 and written with its console, power, interface, front and rear port, module-bay and device-bay templates; when it cannot be fetched the op fails with library_unavailable. With `manufacturer` and `model` it is recorded by hand for a model the library does not hold, and tagged rw-unverified; a part number that is the library's for another model of that maker is refused. A device type NetBox already holds (the same model, under any usual name of its manufacturer, or with the part number as its model) is matched instead (no_change); one it holds with no component template at all is filled with the library's templates (ok, with the counts as `after`).

library_file.description: The file of the index row, <manufacturer folder>/<file>.

AddModuleTypeOp.description: A module type in NetBox (2.5.0), as add_device_type: imported from the pinned device-type library with `library_file`, or, for a module the library does not hold, recorded by hand with `manufacturer` and `model` (no templates) and tagged rw-unverified.

CreateDeviceOp.description: A new device (2.5.0); status active. `role` is a role's name: an existing role of that name is used, else it is created. With `unverified` the device is tagged rw-unverified (its serial does not look like the vendor's and the player confirmed it).

SetDeviceTypeOp.description: Gives an existing device another device type (2.5.0), only where nothing recorded is lost: every port, bay and other component the device has must exist under the same name in the new type, and the new height must fit where the device is racked. The components the device lacks are then added from the type's templates; none is removed or changed. Anything else is refused with the reason.

InstallModuleOp.description: A module fitted in an empty module bay of a device (2.5.0); NetBox adds the module type's ports to the device.

SetPartNumberOp.description: Sets the part number of a device type NetBox holds to the one the pinned device-type library lists for that manufacturer and model (2.5.0). `part_number` is what was read off the label; it is compared without spaces, dashes and case, and the library's own spelling is what is written. Refused when the library does not hold the model or lists no single part number for it (a pattern such as 7X0x is not one), or when `part_number` is not the library's (validation_failed, with details.expected).

MarkUnverifiedOp.description: Tags a device or device type rw-unverified (2.5.0): its serial or model could not be checked against the packs. The tag is created when NetBox has none.

PackInfo.description: One pack the game ships with (2.5.0): what it is, how complete, and where it came from.

entries.description: Providers, device and module types, or rules in the pack.

errors.description: Why the packs could not be used (they did not validate); empty when all is well.

import_from.description: Where a full definition comes from when a player imports a model: a local copy, the pinned commit over HTTPS, or nowhere (imports are unavailable).

status.description: verified = the device-type library holds this maker and model, and no part number contradicts it (a part number the library merely does not list for the model is said in the note, not held against it); mismatch = NetBox holds it under the part number of another model of that maker (note says which); unverified = the library does not hold the model, or it is tagged rw-unverified.

Catalogue.description: The device catalogue (2.5.0): the manufacturers and device types of the player's own NetBox as a collection, with those the device-type library confirms marked verified. Derived from NetBox on every read; the game store only remembers when each type was first seen.
